priorStories.headline: Nearly 1.5 million are displaced in Haiti
priorStories.body:
The International Organization for Migration said nearly 1.5 million people were internally displaced in Haiti. Almost 80% are now living outside Port-au-Prince.

Displacement has risen sharply in the Artibonite region as armed groups expand into rural areas. Recent attacks in Kenscoff displaced more than 4,000 people, the UN agency said.

priorStories.headline: FBI breach exposed personnel medical records
priorStories.body:
Documents reviewed by Reuters supported hackers’ claims that stolen FBI data included psychiatric and other medical evaluation records belonging to personnel.

The ShinyHunters group said it obtained two to three terabytes through FBIjobs.gov, but that volume and the breach’s full scope have not been verified. The FBI declined to discuss the records and said it was investigating the reported breach.

priorStories.headline: Three countries bar Iranian airlines
priorStories.body:
The United Arab Emirates, Oman and Iraq barred Iranian airlines in response to new U.S. sanctions, restricting service by Iranian carriers to three neighboring countries.

An adviser to Iran’s supreme leader threatened that countries maintaining restrictions could lose access to flights and airport services. The measures came amid continuing regional conflict and escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

priorStories.headline: Tigray communications cut amid renewed fighting
priorStories.body:
Internet and telephone service was disrupted in Ethiopia’s Tigray region amid renewed fighting involving federal and Tigrayan forces. Sources gave conflicting accounts of responsibility for the shutdown.

The extent of the combat remained unclear. Ethiopia’s military said hundreds of opposing fighters had been killed or wounded, but Reuters could not independently confirm that claim.

priorStories.headline: Supreme Court again blocks Missouri congressional map
priorStories.body:
The U.S. Supreme Court suspended lower-court decisions that would have required Missouri to use a congressional map redrawn by Republicans for the November midterm elections.

The action was the court’s third intervention in the dispute and again blocked the map, which dismantled a Democratic-held Kansas City district. Litigation over the districts continues.
